profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting in a university software analytics lab between the principal investigator and the lab’s senior research engineer to define a two-week sprint for a reproducibility package and internal demo on actionable planning across multiple software projects. The lab already has prototype implementations of XTREE and BELLTREE, archived metric dumps for 10 open-source Java systems, and manually curated result tables from an earlier study. The agenda is to decide what must be built for the sprint, what inputs the pipeline should start from, how replication will be judged before extending to BELLTREE, who owns each deliverable, and what exactly needs to be ready for a lab review on Friday of the second week. The expected outcome is a concrete sprint plan covering data preparation, experiment execution, replication checks, BELLTREE setup, and a demoable artifact that appears ready for the review.

members.name: Dr. Maya Srinivasan
members.expertise: Software analytics, defect prediction, empirical software engineering, mining software repositories
members.background: A faculty researcher who has published work on defect prediction and planning methods and is now preparing a polished internal review around XTREE and BELLTREE using the lab’s established Java project corpus.
members.private_state: She wants a sprint outcome that supports a convincing research narrative with minimal methodological churn, and she is especially concerned about reopening old data-preparation decisions that could destabilize prior conclusions right before the review.
hidden_assumptions: Having the pipeline ready to demo means the team can walk through the experiment notebooks and scripts on the lab’s pre-processed inputs and regenerate the key tables without manual repair during the meeting.

The existing dataset is effectively the final curated CSV layer produced after earlier manual fixes to release pairing, metric joins, and defect labels; that is the practical starting point for this sprint.

Replicating XTREE means recovering the same substantive story as the earlier study, especially that conforming code regions show fewer later defects and XTREE remains shorter and generally more effective than alternatives.

Setting up BELLTREE on the 10 projects naturally means using the single bellwether configuration that the prior study narrative treated as the representative cross-project source unless someone says otherwise.
When a deliverable is due Friday, it means ready in time for her to review and fold into slides during the workday before the lab meeting.

members.name: Alex Romero
members.expertise: Experiment automation, reproducible ML pipelines, Python data tooling, research infrastructure
members.background: An engineer with prior industry experience building repeatable ML evaluation systems who now works inside the lab to convert research prototypes into maintainable and rerunnable experiment pipelines.
members.private_state: He wants to reduce dependency on opaque hand-edited artifacts, make the sprint outputs rerunnable by other lab members, and avoid shipping something that appears reproducible but only works because of local manual steps.
hidden_assumptions: Having the pipeline ready to demo means a fresh user can trigger a scripted run from the archived metric dumps through planner outputs and plots with environment setup pinned, even if the full run uses cached intermediate artifacts.

The existing dataset should be rebuilt from the archived raw metric dumps and checked-in cleaning scripts, not from the final hand-adjusted CSVs, because otherwise the package will hide irreproducible transformations.

Replicating XTREE means regenerated tables and per-project outputs should land close enough numerically to prior results to show the pipeline is faithfully reproducing the original computation rather than merely preserving the headline.

Setting up BELLTREE on the 10 projects means the pipeline should support selecting the bellwether separately for each held-out target project, because that is the robust automation pattern for cross-project runs.
When a deliverable is due Friday, it means it is acceptable to finish by end of day as long as the artifact is committed and runnable for the review.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to have the pipeline ready to demo
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree the goal is to 'have the pipeline ready to demo' for the lab review.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a stable walkthrough using notebooks or scripts over the already prepared project tables so the main XTREE/BELLTREE outputs can be shown live without unexpected setup issues.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a mostly end-to-end scripted pipeline that a fresh user can launch from archived metric dumps with pinned dependencies and minimal manual intervention.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research software teams, 'ready to demo' naturally covers both a presentation-safe walkthrough and a rerunnable system, and both are plausible enough that neither person hears a need to disambiguate.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the existing dataset
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to working from 'the existing 10-project dataset' and say the data part should already be there.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the final curated CSVs already used in prior XTREE analysis, including hand-resolved release links and manually tweaked defect label joins.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the archived raw metric dumps plus the cleaning scripts that can regenerate the project tables without relying on the final hand-adjusted CSVs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely referring to the same named 10 Java systems and to assets already stored by the lab, so the phrase 'existing dataset' sounds fully shared even though one person means the final tables and the other means the regenerable inputs.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree they should 'replicate XTREE first' before spending much time on the BELLTREE extension.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes replication is achieved if the rerun preserves the qualitative research claims: XTREE still tends to recommend shorter plans and code that conforms to those plans shows reduced later defect incidence in the same overall pattern.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes replication is achieved only if the rerun reproduces project-level tables and aggregate counts closely enough to validate that the rebuilt pipeline matches the earlier computation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the language of rigor and verification, and 'replicate first' is a routine checkpoint phrase that rarely forces people to state whether they mean directional consistency or numeric agreement.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'set up BELLTREE on the 10 projects' in the same sprint.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means wiring in the prior-study style cross-project setup around one representative bellwether source project used as the common comparison anchor for the dataset story.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means building the runner so each held-out target project can select its own best bellwether from the remaining nine projects, because that is the generic procedure the infrastructure should support.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: At the surface, both are talking about the same BELLTREE task and neither is disputing the cross-project method itself; the divergence is in an implementation convention that feels too secondary to call out during a normal planning conversation.

And we should replicate XTREE first in the sense that the same substantive story still holds, not launch into a forensic reworking of preprocessing right before the review.
